Subject: Redwood SOC 2 scope clarification for procurement

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement and audit teams are working through the vendor intake and have a couple of clarifying asks on your SOC 2 coverage before we move to contract redlines. High level we need:

- Confirmation of the audit period for the Type II report you plan to provide (or a bridge letter if the period doesn't align with our fiscal window).
- A responsibility "manifest" mapping which services Redwood considers managed (Redwood responsibility) vs those handled by your cloud provider / subprocessors (customer/cloud/shared). This should call out KMS, backups, logging/retention, and network boundary controls.
- List of current subprocessors and the most recent SOC/attestation each has (or direct link to their report).

Can you share a CSV or spreadsheet with the manifest and any supporting docs (SOC 2 PDF, bridge letter, or CSP report links)? Our target audit window to cover is 2026-09-01 through 2027-03-31.

Best,
Helen Park
Director, Vendor Risk — Silverline Payments
helen@silverline.com

Ben —

I reviewed the first-pass manifest and added an "ownership" column for each control, plus a short rationale line for KMS and backup responsibilities. A couple of clarifications I added:

- KMS key custody: Redwood manages application-level encryption keys; the CSP manages the underlying HSM service that stores tenant keys. We call this "co-managed" and flagged the controls where customer configuration is required.
- Backups: Redwood triggers snapshots and lifecycle policies, but long-term retention (replication and off-region storage) leverages the cloud provider; noted which retention windows are our responsibility vs the provider.
- Logging: Immediate request/ingest logging is Redwood's; longer-term log archival and the storage encryption-at-rest is the CSP.

I've uploaded the updated CSV to the Drive link in the related_links and marked rows that typically require additional attestation. Please let Helen know we'll follow up with the bridge letter and a pack of subprocessors' latest attestations.

-L

Lauren Bishop
Manager, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
